## READ BEFORE ACTIVATING

Your n8n ALREADY RUNS a P0.2. This file is a rebuild, not a patch.

**Never leave both Active.** Two workflows writing the same tables is
worse than one.

Safe cutover:
  1. Import this. Leave it INACTIVE.
  2. Fill in Config.
  3. Run it once with the Manual Trigger (or the AD4 Workflows page).
  4. Compare its Summary line against your original's.
  5. Only then: deactivate the original, activate this.

## The only thing you have to do

**Open polymarket.com, find any daily temperature market, copy the address bar,
and paste it into `example_event_url` in the Config node.** Then run.

That one link is all this needs. The workflow fetches that event, works out the
slug pattern for every city and every day, and prints the exact line to paste
into `slug_template`. Run once more and it is done.

### Why it asks you instead of searching

The Polymarket endpoints here are **NOT reachable from the build machine** -
that sandbox blocks polymarket.com - so the **first run** is the only test
there is. That is exactly why this asks you for a link rather than asserting
an endpoint.

It tried. Gamma ignores every narrowing parameter this repo could test:

| asked for | got |
|---|---|
| `?limit=200&tag_slug=weather` | assumed 200 |
| `?limit=40` | **2160 events, 26 MB** - n8n ran out of memory |
| `?closed=false` | **20 events, none of them weather** |

The limit is not honoured and the default page is twenty. The machine that
builds these files is blocked from polymarket.com, so every further attempt is
another guess costing you a run. A link from your own browser is not a guess.

If you leave `example_event_url` empty it will still try: it walks eight pages
looking for temperature slugs, writes nothing, and tells you what it found. It
also notices when paging is being ignored, which looks like "there are only
twenty markets" and is not.

### What to check on the first successful run

**The settlement dates** in the Summary. They come from `endDate` rolled back a
day when it lands before noon UTC, which is how these markets close. If they
are all one day out, that rule is one function at the top of
`Parse markets + bands`.

**"bucket label(s) unreadable"**. Polymarket states the bucket only as text -
"70-71F", "78F or above" - and a band with no numeric bounds cannot be priced
by anything. A handful is normal; most of them means the format moved, and the
run stops rather than writing a ladder with holes in it.
